A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, Appendices A–K, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison despite pagination and display-placement changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original data-dropping analyses of LLM leaderboards and sports rankings, including deletion thresholds, random-deletion trials and qualitative preference analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and the appendices, including Tables 1–4 and the preference case studies.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains score-gap ordering, AMIP subset selection and exact refitting; its dataset and index notation is rewritten. The additive one-step Newton option remains in Appendix C.3 despite its removal from Section 5.2's summary.

E1.justification: Both versions analyze Chatbot, Vision, Webdev and Search Arenas, MT-bench, NBA and ATP tennis, with the same human- and LLM-judged variants. No dataset, task or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons are retained, including uniform-random deletion in Appendix A.3. The new discussion of Perlitz et al. (2024) is related work, not an added empirical comparator.

E3.justification: The tested k values, dataset filtering, deletion fractions and refitting procedures remain unchanged (Sections 4.1, A.3 and D). Newly specifying the bootstrap confidence level does not establish a change to the existing experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both versions retain bootstrap-ranking sensitivity, random-deletion controls, player-involvement analysis, preference case studies, score-margin ablations and verification of identified subsets (Appendices A and E–G). Display relocation does not add analyses.

E5.justification: Figures 3–9 newly specify that the bootstrap confidence intervals are 95%; v2 leaves that level unstated. The plotted intervals and reporting of 100 uniform-deletion trials are retained, without evidence of additional runs or revised estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Section 5.1 corrects 0.0003% to 0.003%, aligning the prose with Table 1's unchanged 2 of 57,477 preferences (0.00348%). Tables 1–4 and plotted results are retained. A new footnote also reports that no ties were observed in BT point estimates.

T1.justification: Definition 2 changes the top-k set from full-data score values to player indices under arbitrary weights, correcting its membership semantics. v3 also explicitly assumes untied point estimates for the main exposition. Appendix B's proposition and proof remain score-valued, leaving a mismatch with the revised definition.

C1.justification: The introduction removes the categorical assertion that no suitable method exists beyond brute-force search. The main methodological contribution and headline claims about tiny deletions, MT-bench robustness and human-versus-LLM judging remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The introduction removes its characterization of the goal as providing an upper bound on the degree of non-robustness. A new footnote clarifies the scope of untied point rankings versus handled bootstrap-ranking ties. Mechanism explanations and masking/false-negative limitations remain.

D1.justification: Dataset identifiers and filters, hardware/runtime information, and the GPT-5.1 judging prompt and access disclosure are retained (Sections 3, D and F). The pseudocode edits clarify equivalent notation without introducing implementation procedures or changing resource access.

R1.justification: Section 5.1 adds Perlitz et al. (2024) and discusses manipulation of absolute-score/Mean Win Rate rankings, distinguishing that setting from pairwise-preference rankings. The introduction moderates its novelty statement; several other reference changes merely update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized introduction and method rewrites, clarifies data-weight notation, moves the rank explanation, and corrects grammar, terminology and an author email. The main section order and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: All 18 figures and four tables are retained, and all 23 embedded images are identical. Bootstrap captions add 95%; Algorithm 1 and several tables move, and the sports-ranking figures share a page. These are limited caption and layout changes.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through the corrected top-k membership definition, the percentage correction, explicit confidence levels and additional related-work context. The gains are limited because empirical support is unchanged and Appendix B's score-valued proof was not updated to match the revised index-valued definition.
